  description: This item defines the lookback period for checking duplicates, storing the interval as a string value in days. The value is converted to hours and stored in item-17220 Inpatient Duplicate Interval; positive numbers indicate days, while fractions represent hours (e.g., .25 for 6 hours), and values followed by 'W' indicate weeks (e.g., 3W for 3 weeks). The system converts these inputs to days for display, and large values may significantly impact performance, so consultation with a Technical Services Representative is advised before setting them. When a procedure is ordered, the system checks if it was previously ordered within the specified duplicate interval and prompts the user for confirmation if a duplicate is found.

This rule may connect to a single non-attending provider who was either the first, last, or longest-serving member of the patient's treatment team, with options to filter by specific treatment team roles or exclude non-ED treatment team members, identifying the member with the most significant impact on the ED aspect of the patient's encounter.

  description: The unique provider ID for the key nurse associated with this encounter is defined by the rule: RESPONSIBLE NURSE (49368). — emr|dbo|ED_ENCOUNTERS_DM|KEY_RESIDENT_ID
  description: The unique provider ID associated with the key resident for this encounter is defined by the rule: RESPONSIBLE RESIDENT (49731). This rule may connect to a single non-attending provider who was either the first, last, or longest-serving member of the patient's treatment team, with options to filter by specific treatment team roles or exclude non-ED treatment team members, identifying the member with the most significant impact on the ED aspect of the patient's encounter.

The new column, FINAL_DX_POA_CODE, will connect to a new category table ZC_DX_POA and should be utilized starting Spring 2008. — emr|dbo|HOSPITAL_ENCOUNTERS|MU_HOSP_ADMSN_TIME
  description: This field records the date and time of the patient's admission to inpatient care or when they were roomed in the ED. It first checks if the source item is populated; if so, it captures the moment the patient was first admitted. If not, it assesses the version of the standard unique patient denominator in use (LSD 34062) and the patient's ED status. If the denominator is for all ED patients, this field will contain the hospital admission date and time. If the patient was neither inpatient nor seen in the ED, the field will be null. If the denominator is for ED to Observation patients only and the patient was seen in the ED as an observation patient, this field will be populated with the hospital admission date and time. Additionally, if the encounter pertains to a newborn and there are settings to exclude newborns, this field will be null.

If the ordered dose exceeds this percentage difference from the nearest standard dose, it will not be converted to a standard dose. For instance, if set to 50 percent and an ordered dose is 100 mg, it could be adjusted to a standard dose of 60 mg or 150 mg, but not to 40 mg or 160 mg. If this field is empty, the percentage defined in system settings (Medication, Allergy, Imm, etc. > Dosing, Rate Calculation > Dosing Calculations 2) will apply. If that field is also empty, all ordered doses will be rounded to the nearest standard doses without regard to percentage deviation.

Discrepancies may occur if the patient can only afford a smaller supply or if the pharmacy has a limited stock of the medication available for dispensing.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_DISP_QTYUNT_CODE
  description: When a prescription is filled at an integrated pharmacy, a FILL_CONTACT is generated in the order, and all related fill details are recorded in this FILL_CONTACT. A prescription may have several fills. The ACTUAL_AMOUNT_DISPENSED represents the quantity the pharmacy provides, which may differ from the INTENDED_QUANTITY that the prescriber intended for the patient. Discrepancies can occur if the patient can only afford a smaller supply or if the pharmacy has a limited stock of the medication available.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_INT_QTY
  description: When a prescription is filled in an integrated pharmacy, a FILL_CONTACT is generated in the order, and all fill details are recorded in this FILL_CONTACT. A prescription may have several fills, representing the quantity the prescriber intended for the patient. In instances of partial fills, the patient may pay for a reduced supply, or the pharmacy may have a limited quantity of the medication available, with the actual amount dispensed recorded in DISPENSE_QUANTITY.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_INT_QTYUNT_CODE
  description: When a prescription is filled at an integrated pharmacy, a FILL_CONTACT is generated in the order, and all related fill details are recorded in this FILL_CONTACT. A prescription may have several fills. The amount unit reflects the quantity the prescriber intended for the patient. In instances of partial fills, the patient may pay for a reduced supply, or the pharmacy may have a limited quantity of the medication available, with the actual dispensed amount recorded in DISPENSE_QUANTITY.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_INT_SUP_DAYS
  description: When a prescription is filled in an integrated pharmacy, a FILL_CONTACT is generated in the order, and all related fill information is recorded in this FILL_CONTACT. A prescription may have several fills, and if the fill is a partial fill, it indicates the number of days the dispensed supply will last. For instance, a partial fill of 15 tablets for a daily medication would have an intended days supply of 15.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_IS_PARTIAL_FLAG
  description: When a prescription is filled at an integrated pharmacy, a FILL_CONTACT is created in the order, and all related fill information is recorded in this FILL_CONTACT. A prescription may have multiple fills, and this item indicates whether the fill is partial. If the patient can only afford a smaller quantity or if the pharmacy has a limited supply of the medication, the dispensed amount may differ from the intended amount specified by the prescriber. For instance, if a patient has a fill for 30 tablets intended for a 30-day supply, a partial fill of 15 tablets will provide a 15-day supply, with the remainder available for later pickup when the patient can pay or when more stock is available. This flag is also utilized in adjudication to inform the insurer that the fill is partial, prompting an adjustment in the payment amount.

A prescription may have several fills, and the value is utilized in adjudication to specify which fill is being adjudicated. The fill numbers are sequential, starting with the first fill as 0 and subsequent refills numbered from 1 to 99.

— emr|dbo|ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO|FILL_PAT_LOC_CODE

Typically, this location is "Outpatient" for in-pharmacy services, "Home" for mail orders, and for long-term care, it may be "Nursing Home," "Long Term/Extended Care," "Rest Home," "Boarding Home," "Skilled Care Facility," or "Hospice," depending on the patient's situation and payor requirements during adjudication.

  description: The column PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_1 and PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_2 is still available but should not be used; instead, utilize the column ADDRESS in table PAT_ADDRESS. The new table PAT_ADDRESS allows access to all lines of a patient's permanent address, while the previous columns only provided the first two lines; PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_1 and PATIENTS.ADD_LINE_2 remain active to avoid disrupting existing custom reports. To access the new column, join PATIENTS.PATIENT_ID with PAT_ADDRESS on PATIENT_ID to retrieve the ADDRESS and LINE values, where each PATIENT_ID corresponds to a unique patient and each LINE value corresponds to a specific line of that patient's address.

  description: The column is still available but is not recommended for use; instead, utilize the column TEMP_ADDRESS in table PAT_TEMP_ST_ADDR. The table PAT_TEMP_ST_ADDR provides access to all lines of a patient's temporary address. The columns PATIENTS.TMP_ADDR_LINE_1 and PATIENTS.TMP_ADDR_LINE_2 have not been deprecated to avoid disrupting any custom reports that rely on them. The table PAT_TEMP_ST_ADDR provides access to all lines of a patient's temporary address. The columns PATIENTS.TMP_ADDR_LINE_1 and PATIENTS.TMP_ADDR_LINE_2 have not been deprecated to avoid disrupting any custom reports that rely on them. To access the new column, join column PATIENTS.PATIENT_ID with table PAT_TEMP_ST_ADDR on column PATIENT_ID to retrieve the TEMP_ADDRESS and LINE values, where each PATIENT_ID corresponds to a unique patient and each LINE value indicates a specific line of that patient's temporary address.

To retrieve the value previously held in the AGE column after the EMR system upgrade, join PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.PATIENT_ID with PATIENTS.PATIENT_ID and compute the difference between PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.CONTACT_DATE and PATIENTS.BIRTH_DATE. The CONTACT_DATE may not always represent the most relevant date for the encounter; for instance, for admissions, you can join PATIENTS.PATIENT_ID with HOSPITAL_ENCOUNTERS.PATIENT_ID and calculate the difference between HOSPITAL_ENCOUNTERS.HOSP_ADMSN_TIME or HOSPITAL_ENCOUNTERS.HOSP_DISCH_TIME and PATIENTS.BIRTH_DATE.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|LOS_PRIME_PROC_ID
  description: The ID of the procedure record associated with the primary LOS_CODE for this encounter. This is not the CPT_CODE and serves as an internal identifier that is generally not accessible to users.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|LOS_PROC_CODE
  description: The procedure code associated with the primary LOS (level of service).

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|NONCVRED_SERVICE_FLAG
  description: A flag that indicates if the appointment is for a service not included in the patient's coverage benefits. It is marked as "Y" when the service is not covered and "N" when it is covered.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|ORDERING_PROV_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the ordering provider associated with an appointment, as recorded on the Orders form within the Appointment Info activity.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|ORDERING_PROV_TEXT
  description: Data from a free text field that includes details about the provider who submitted the order.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|OUTGOING_CALL_FLAG
  description: Specifies if a call related to a telephone encounter was made by the patient or the clinic/hospital. A "Y" denotes an outgoing call from the clinic/hospital, while an "N" signifies an incoming call from the patient.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PATIENT_ENC_DATE_REAL
  description: A unique contact date represented in decimal format. The integer part indicates the date of contact, while the digits following the decimal point differentiate multiple contacts on the same date, with each contact being unique; for instance, .00 represents the first or only contact, .01 represents the second contact, and so on.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PATIENT_ID
  description: The unique identifier assigned to the patient record. This ID may be encrypted if the use of the enterprise reporting encryption utility has been selected.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PCP_PROV_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the provider record of the patient's General Primary Care Provider at the time of the encounter. This ID may be encrypted if the security utility for enterprise reporting has been selected.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PHONE_REM_STAT_CODE
  description: This represents the status provided by an automated appointment reminder system, with typical values including CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, BUSY, etc. This item is configured by batch templates 91 and 96.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PHON_CALL_FLAG
  description: When this flag is enabled, it prevents all phone calls associated with this appointment. A null value in this column signifies that no user had the option to block a phone call for this contact, which may be due to: (a) the contact not being an appointment, (b) the appointment being created prior to the introduction of this feature, or (c) the department not utilizing the standard Appointment Demographics node in its After Appointment Entry Advantage Activity.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PHON_NUM_APPT
  description: The phone number designated for receiving all calls related to this appointment.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PRIMARY_LOC_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the patient's primary location at the time of the encounter. Note: This may differ from the patient's current primary location.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|PULSE
  description: The PULSE measurement of the patient recorded during this encounter.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|REFERRAL_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the referral record associated with this appointment.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|REFERRAL_REQ_FLAG
  description: A flag that indicates if a referral is necessary for an appointment based on visit coverage. It is marked as “Y” when a referral is required and “N” when it is not.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|REFERRAL_SOURCE_ID
  description: The REFERRAL_ID number of the referring physician, who may belong to an external organization.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|RESPIRATIONS
  description: The RESPIRATION_RATE of the patient as noted during this encounter.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|ROUTE_SUM_PRNT_FLAG
  description: A flag indicating whether the routing summary was printed at the time of the enterprise reporting extract. This column can have a value of Y (printed) or N (not printed), with the default value set to N.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|SERVICE_AREA_ID
  description: The connection to the SERVICE_AREA for the ENCOUNTER.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|SIGN_IN_TIME
  description: The date and time when the patient checked in for the appointment related to this encounter. The date is always the appointment date, irrespective of the actual check-in date, and the time can be adjusted by users in the application, which may differ from the system-audited time. For the system-recorded check-in time, refer to the SIGNIN_AUD_DTTM column in PATIENT_ENC_7.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|SIGN_IN_USER_ID
  description: The unique identifier of the system user who signed in the patient for this encounter. This field will be NULL if the encounter has not undergone the Sign In process, and the ID may be encrypted.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|SURGICAL_SVC_CODE
  description: The category value related to the surgical service for this patient contact.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|TEMPERATURE
  description: The temperature of the patient recorded during this encounter. This value is expressed in degrees Fahrenheit, irrespective of the method used to enter the temperature reading.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG
  description: In the PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table, the TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG column is no longer in use and has been replaced by the TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG column in the PATIENT_ENC4 table. To retrieve the value of the deprecated column after the EMR system upgrade, join PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG with PATIENT_ENC4.TOBACCO_USE_VRFY_FLAG.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|UPDATE_DATE
  description: The timestamp when this patient encounter was included in enterprise reporting.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VISIT_EPM_ID
  description: This column is populated solely for indemnity coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 1) and contains the unique identifier of the payor linked to the coverage record. For managed care coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 2), join COVERAGE.COVERAGE_ID with V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.COVERAGE_ID and apply filters on V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.EFF_DATE and V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.TERM_DATE to retrieve the corresponding PAYOR_ID.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VISIT_EPP_ID
  description: This column is populated solely for indemnity coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 1) and contains the unique identifier for the benefit plan linked to the coverage record. For managed care coverages (COVERAGE_TYPE_C equal to 2), join COVERAGE.COVERAGE_ID with V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.COVERAGE_ID and apply filters on V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.EFF_DATE and V_COVERAGE_PAYOR_PLAN.TERM_DATE to identify the corresponding BENEFIT_PLAN_ID.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VISIT_FC
  description: The financial class associated with this coverage is utilized solely for CMS claims forms and may not be consistently populated for reporting purposes. Reporting should be conducted using the financial class of the payor indicated in this coverage.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VISIT_PROV_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the visit provider linked to this encounter. If multiple providers are associated with one encounter, this ID refers to the first provider in the list. This item may be NULL if no provider is present for this encounter, and the ID may be encrypted.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VISIT_PROV_TITLE
  description: The title of the visit provider. Refer to VISIT_PROV_ID above for the definition of visit provider.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|VST_SPECIAL_NEEDS_CODE
  description: This field records any specific requirements for a visit.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|WC_TPL_VISIT_CMT
  description: Comments associated with the expected account type are stored in the SOURCE_ITEM.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|WC_TPL_VISIT_CODE
  description: A field that specifies if the patient's contact pertains to a workers compensation or third party liability case.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS|WEIGHT
  description: The patient's weight recorded during this encounter is stored in ounces, regardless of the input method. To convert this value to pounds, divide the number by 16.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|ADT_BED_ENC

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|ADT_ROOM_NM_WID

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|ENCOUNTER_NUM

  description: The CATEGORY value that indicates the type of the event record.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|IN_DTTM
  description: The moment the patient was transferred to the department/room/bed.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|OUT_DTTM
  description: The column PATIENT_OUT_DTTM indicates the moment the patient was transferred out of the department/room/bed. If the patient remains in the department/room/bed, this column will not provide a value.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY|PATIENT_OUT_DTTM
  description: This column records the exact moment the patient was transferred out of the department/room/bed. If the patient remains in the department/room/bed, this column will not contain any value, while the column OUT_DTTM will show the time of transfer or the current time if the patient is still present.

  description: This column contains a value of 1 if the dispense preparation was initiated but not finished in the Dispense Preparation activity; otherwise, it holds a value of 0. A dispense is deemed started if either of the following warnings appeared during preparation: 35016 - "Dispense Prep Order Discontinued or Completed" or 35017 - "Dispense Prep Order Past End Time.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE|DISP_PREP_COMPLETED_BOOL
  description: This column contains a value of 1 if the dispense was successfully completed during the Dispense Preparation activity; otherwise, it contains a value of 0.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE|DISP_PREP_HOUR

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE|DISP_PREP_NEAR_MISS_BOOL
  description: This column shows if the dispense preparation included a near miss. A near miss is identified when a warning triggers, prompting the user to cancel and restart the action. The warning types evaluated for near misses are: 35010 - Dispense Prep NDC Not Part of Order and 35011 - Dispense Prep NDC Expired.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE|DISP_PREP_NOT_ATTEMPTED_BOOL
  description: This column contains a value of 0 if a dispense was either prepared or attempted during the Dispense Preparation activity, or if dispense preparation data was obtained from an external system. If neither condition is met, it holds a value of 1.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|FIRST_SCHED_DUE_TIME_DTTM
  description: The initial scheduled due time for the medication order. If modified during order verification, it is updated to reflect the new date and time.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|FIRST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL
  description: The unique internal date of the first verification contact for the order. This column is often used to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|FIRST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL_LINE
  description: The line number for the data related to the most recent action in the verification queue during the order verification process. If the order has been verified, this represents the verification audit trail associated with FIRST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL and is often used to connect to the RX_VERIFY_TRACE table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|FREQ_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the discrete frequency record related to this medication order. This column is commonly used to connect to the IP_FREQUENCY table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|FREQ_NAME
  description: The designation of the order frequency.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|INITIATED_DTTM
  description: This column records the date and time when a conditional order was initiated.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|IS_RELEASED_FLAG
  description: This indicates if an order has been released. Unreleased orders lack a report date, so when using the REPORT_DATE column for a date range, signed and held orders will be automatically excluded.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|IVENT_FLAG
  description: Specifies if an intervention has been recorded for this order. A "Y" signifies that at least one intervention is documented, while an "N" indicates that no interventions are recorded.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|LAST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL
  description: The unique internal contact date of the most recent verification contact for the order initiated by a user. This date pertains to the last verification contact where MEDICATION_ORDERS.MED_VERIFY_TYPE_CODE is not 4-Modify On Patient Transfer, 5-Modify On Order Transfer, or 6-NDC replacement. This column is often used to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table for details on changes made to orders that have undergone reverification. The last verification contact, irrespective of verify type, is available in ORDER_RXVER_NOADSN.LAST_VERIFY_DATE_REAL.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|MEDICATION_ID
  description: Columns with Medication IDs in MEDICATION_ORDERS and its related addendum tables may include Orderable records or templates that do not correspond to actual medications. It is advisable to utilize this column for reporting on medication orders, and if your search involves mixture components, ensure to also query ORDER_MEDMIXINFO.MEDICATION_ID alongside this column.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|MEDICATION_NAME
  description: The name assigned to the medication.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|NF_POST_VERIFY_FLAG
  description: Indicates if a medication order has been confirmed by the pharmacist as non-formulary. A "Y" signifies that the pharmacist has verified the order as non-formulary. To identify orders placed as non-formulary, refer to the NF_PRE_VERIFY_FLAG column. A NULL value indicates that the order was either rejected or not verified.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|NF_PRE_VERIFY_FLAG
  description: Indicates if the order was submitted as non-formulary before verification. A "Y" signifies a non-formulary medication.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|NON_CLINICAL_OVERRIDE_FLAG
  description: This column indicates whether the order was a non-clinical override in the case of an ADS override. Non-clinical overrides result in charge-only orders that are not displayed on the MAR.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ONE_STEP_MED_FLAG
  description: Indicates if the ORDER is a one-step medication, meaning its administration is recorded in a single step.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ON_THE_FLY_FLAG
  description: This indicates whether a medication order is made on-the-fly by nurses. An on-the-fly medication order is created by scanning an NDC, as opposed to an ADS override, which involves pulling a drug from an ADS cabinet to generate a new order interface message.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERABLE_MED_ID
  description: This column contains the medication ID of the Orderable record if a medication was ordered using an IMS orderable for Mixtures or Drips. It is primarily intended for searching the usage of specific Orderables.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERING_DATE
  description: The date associated with ORDERING_DTTM.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERING_DATE_REAL
  description: The unique internal contact date for the ordering contact associated with the order. This column is often utilized to connect to the ORDER_DISPENSE_INFO table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERING_DTTM
  description: The date and time when the order was released. For other order types created on the fly, such as override pulls, one step medications, and bulk charges, this represents the time the order was created.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERING_HOUR
  description: The hour of the day represented by ORDERING_DTTM.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDERING_PROV_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the provider who issued the medication order, typically associated with the PROVIDERS table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_DOSE
  description: The specific dose of a medication input by the user during the orders activity.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_END_DTTM
  description: The END_DATE_TIME of the order.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_HISTORY_LINK_NM_WID
  description: A reference to the Order History activity for the EMR system-Crystal Integration, represented as RX_ORDER_NM_WID.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_MED_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the medication order.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_PRIORITY
  description: The name of the category for the order priority.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_PRIORITY_CODE
  description: The category number indicating the priority level assigned to an order.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_ROUTE
  description: The sequence in which the route of administration is applied.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|ORDER_START_DTTM
  description: The date and time when the order was initiated.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PATIENT_DEPT_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the patient department at the time the order was issued. For override pulls and bulk charges, this corresponds to the dispense department of the order. If the order's department is unavailable, the department from the order's encounter is utilized instead (PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS.EFFECTIVE_DEPT_ID).

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PATIENT_DEPT_NAME
  description: The name of the patient department when the order was issued. For override pulls, this refers to the dispense department associated with the order.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PATIENT_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the patient record associated with this line. This column is often utilized to connect to the PATIENTS table.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PATIENT_LOCATION_ID
  description: The unique identifier for the revenue location associated with the patient department when the order was generated or released.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PATIENT_LOCATION_NAME
  description: The name of the revenue location associated with the patient department when the order was either released or created.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|PRN_FLAG
  description: This indicates if a frequency is classified as PRN (as needed).

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|QUEUE_REASON
  description: The name of the final queue reason. The potential values are detailed in the description for RXQ_REASON_CODE.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|RELEASING_USER_ID
  description: The user responsible for releasing the order.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|REPORT_DATE
  description: The date when the order was released; for conditional orders, this represents the initiation time. If the conditional order was not initiated, the value is null. This column is often utilized as a date range in reports.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|RXQ_REASON_CODE
  description: The CATEGORY_ID of the last reason the order entered the verify queue during the initial order verification process. Possible values include 1-New, 11-Override Pull, 15-First Verify, 16-2nd Verify, 17-Conditional, 18-Conditional 1rst, 19-Conditional 2nd, 20-Conditional Initiate, 23-Review On-The-Fly, or 25-Deferred.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|RX_ORDER_NAME
  description: The ORDER_NAME is derived from multiple potential sources, prioritized as follows: DISPLAY_NAME, ORDER_DESCRIPTION, and lastly, the MEDICATION_NAME.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|RX_ORDER_NM_WID
  description: A unique identifier for an order formed by combining RX_ORDER_NAME and the order ID. This column is frequently utilized for grouping, sorting, and presentation in reports.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|RX_UNQUEUE_REAS_CODE
  description: The CATEGORY_ID of the last unqueue reason or action performed by a user during the initial order verification process, which may be 1-Verified or 2-Rejected.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|UNQUEUE_REASON
  description: The identifier for the most recent unqueue action taken by a user in the initial order verification process. The potential values are detailed in the description for RX_UNQUEUE_REAS_CODE.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DATE
  description: The date associated with VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM
  description: The date and time when the order was placed in the verify queue for the reason specified in QUEUE_REASON.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_HOUR
  description: The hour of the day for the column VERIFY_QUEUE_ENTRY_DTTM.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_QUEUE_LOGIN_DEPT_ID
  description: This item contains the login department of the user who is being verified, as recorded in the source item.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_QUEUE_USER_ID
  description: The user who performed the action that resulted in the order being removed from the verify queue.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DATE
  description: The date associated with VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM
  description: The date and time when the user performed the action that led to the unqueue reason specified in UNQUEUE_REASON.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER|VERIFY_UNQUEUE_HOUR
  description: The hour component of VERIFY_UNQUEUE_DTTM.

=== table (90) ===

— emr|dbo|ADT_EVENTS
  description: The ADT_EVENTS table serves as the primary repository for ADT event history data. It includes multiple foreign keys referencing other ADT tables.

— emr|dbo|ALERT_ACTIONS
  description: User actions performed in response to alerts.

— emr|dbo|ALERT_HISTORY
  description: This table holds general historical data for various medication warnings or advisories, capturing information each time a warning is activated during different activities. To obtain patient details, connect this table to the CLINICAL_ALERTS table, which can then be linked to the PATIENTS or PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS table; for order-related information, link to ALT_ORDINFO. For specific medication or condition details related to each warning type, connect to relevant tables such as ALT_DRUG_ALLERGY for drug-allergy warnings, ALT_DRUG_DFALC for drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-alcohol warnings, ALT_DRUG_DUPTHERPY and ALT_DRUG_DUPTHYMED for duplicate therapy warnings, ALT_DRUG_IV and ALT_DRUG_IVMED for IV warnings, and ALT_DRUG_PREGNANCY and ALT_DRUG_PREGMED for pregnancy warnings.

— emr|dbo|BED_CONFIG
  description: This table contains the information from the Hospital Beds (BED) master file.

— emr|dbo|CALENDAR_DATES
  description: This table functions like a standard "Date Dimension" in a Data Warehouse. By linking your dates to this table, you can prevent the need for date functions to be processed on the reporting server, which can be slow as it typically retrieves all rows and filters them in memory. This table streamlines the process and allows you to utilize the EMR database as if it were a data warehouse.

— emr|dbo|CLINICAL_ALERTS
  description: The CLINICAL_ALERTS table holds a single record for each alert generated in the clinical application. Each record is identified by the alert ID and includes essential details about the alert, including the patient, patient ENC, alert type, and user visibility status.

— emr|dbo|CLINICAL_NOTES
  description: This table holds general information from General Use Notes items, emphasizing time-insensitive data that is recorded once per item. Other note tables, such as NOTES_ACCT and CODING_CLA_NOTES, store data for various types of notes.

— emr|dbo|CLINICAL_NOTE_TEXT
  description: The CLINICAL_NOTE_TEXT table stores the free-text body of clinical notes, one row per note text segment, linked to note metadata by note ID.

— emr|dbo|CONFIG_GROUPER_CATEGORIES
  description: This table holds information regarding groupers of category values.

— emr|dbo|DEPARTMENTS
  description: The DEPARTMENTS table holds general information regarding departments.

— emr|dbo|DIAGNOSES
  description: The DIAGNOSES table holds fundamental details regarding diagnoses.

— emr|dbo|DIAGNOSES_CURRENT_ICD10
  description: The DIAGNOSES_CURRENT_ICD10 table maps internal diagnosis records to their current ICD-10 codes, one row per diagnosis-to-code mapping.

— emr|dbo|ED_ENCOUNTERS_DM
  description: ED_ENCOUNTERS_DM is a data mart table that holds essential information regarding a patient's stay in the emergency department (ED). It combines date and time columns for calculating turnaround times, and data is populated only when the ED Encounters registry (R HFR 49003) is activated, capturing only those patient encounters that meet the registry's inclusion criteria. Important Note: This table includes a special staging override code that is applicable only for incremental extracts; a full extract should not be performed as it will erase historical data from the table, potentially permanently.

— emr|dbo|ED_ENCOUNTERS_FACT
  description: The ED_ENCOUNTERS_FACT table contains frequently utilized data for emergency department encounters, with each encounter represented by a single row. Encounters that are either pending or cancelled are excluded from this table.

— emr|dbo|ED_EVENT_INFO
  description: This table holds data regarding the current event records.

— emr|dbo|ED_EVENT_TEMPLATES

— emr|dbo|ED_PATIENT_INFO
  description: This table holds data that aids in associating records (such as PATIENT, DEPARTMENT, etc.) with their corresponding events.

— emr|dbo|EMPLOYEES

  description: This table holds hospital account data from the Hospital Accounts Receivable master file. — emr|dbo|PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS
  description: The PATIENT_ENCOUNTER table holds a single record for each patient encounter in the system. By default, it excludes Registration and PCP/Clinic Change contacts (encounter types 1 and 31) but includes all appointments, office visits, telephone encounters, and other encounter types. The primary key for the PATIENT_ENCOUNTER table is ENCOUNTER_ID. Additionally, there is an index named EIX_FILT_PATIENT_ENC_RFL on the REFERRAL_ID column in Oracle, which is not listed among the indexes; this index is created by EFN_FAUX_RFL_FILT_INX.

— emr|dbo|PATIENT_OR_ADM_LINK
  description: The PATIENT_OR_ADM_LINK table links patient encounters to operating room cases, one row per encounter-to-OR-log link.

— emr|dbo|PROCEDURES_CATALOG
  description: The PROCEDURES_CATALOG table holds fundamental details regarding the procedure records within the system, encompassing both A/R and clinical procedures.

— emr|dbo|PROCEDURE_ORDERS
  description: The PROCEDURE_ORDERS table allows for reporting on the procedures requested within the clinical system, and it includes patient and contact identification details for each entry.

— emr|dbo|PROCEDURE_ORDERS_EXT
  description: The PROCEDURE_ORDERS_EXT table allows for reporting on procedures ordered within the clinical system. It shares a similar structure with PROCEDURE_ORDERS and was established as a third table to avoid increasing the size of ORDER_PROC_2.

— emr|dbo|PROVIDERS
  description: The PROVIDERS table holds essential details regarding your provider records, which can include caregivers, resources, classes, devices, and modalities.

— emr|dbo|REF_ALERT_ACTIONS
  description: This table holds the values representing the actions that a user can perform in response to alerts.

— emr|dbo|REF_ALERT_OVERRIDE_REASONS
  description: Reference table of category values for the reasons a user may select when overriding a clinical alert.

— emr|dbo|REF_ALERT_STATUS
  description: This table contains the categories for alert status. The alert status describes the outcome of an interaction alert after it has been viewed by an end user, with possible statuses including OVERRIDDEN, REMOVED, FILTERED, or CANCELLED.

— emr|dbo|REF_DISCHARGE_DISPOSITION
  description: Reference table of category values for patient discharge dispositions, where or how the patient left the facility at the end of the encounter.

— emr|dbo|REF_ED_DISPOSITION
  description: Reference table of category values for emergency department dispositions, the outcome of the patient's emergency department visit, such as admitted, discharged, or transferred.

— emr|dbo|REF_ETHNIC_GROUP
  description: This table holds the category details for patient ethnic groups.

— emr|dbo|REF_GENERIC_MED
  description: Reference table of generic medication records, linking medication orders to their generic drug identity.

— emr|dbo|REF_PATIENT_CLASS
  description: This table holds the category details for the patient classes associated with the hospital encounter.

— emr|dbo|REF_PATIENT_RACE
  description: This table holds the category details related to patient race.

— emr|dbo|REF_SEX
  description: Reference table of category values for patient sex.

— emr|dbo|REF_SHOWN_PLACE
  description: This table contains the categories for the various locations where alerts may be displayed in the clinical application.

— emr|dbo|RX_VERIFY_TRACE
  description: This table records medication orders that are in the pharmacy verification queue.

— emr|dbo|TREATMENT_TEAMS
  description: The TREATMENT_TEAMS table holds details about inpatient treatment teams, with each entry linked to an ENCOUNTER_ID.

— emr|dbo|VISIT_REASONS
  description: This table holds fundamental details for entries in the REASON_FOR_VISIT (HRV) master file.

— emr|dbo|V_HOSPITAL_TRANSACTIONS
  description: This view simplifies charge homing reporting by excluding non-home charges that have been re-homed and updating billing account IDs to reference the correct billing account record for reporting. It includes hospital account transaction detail information from the HTR master file.

— emr|dbo|V_OR_CASE_LOG
  description: The V_OR_CASE_LOG view reports operating room cases from the surgical log, one row per OR case log, including in-room times.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_ENCOUNTERS
  description: This view simplifies charge homing reporting by excluding non-home charges that have been re-homed and updating billing account IDs to reference the correct billing account record for reporting purposes. The patient encounter table includes one record for each patient encounter in the system, and by default, this view omits Registration and PCP/Clinic Change contacts (Encounter types 1, 31), while including all appointments, office visits, telephone encounters, and other encounter types. The primary key for the patient encounter view is ENCOUNTER_ID.

— emr|dbo|V_PATIENT_LOCATION_HISTORY
  description: A dimensional view designed to identify a patient's department, room, and/or bed at a specific datetime. It includes one row for each admission, transfer in, or leave of absence return ADT event, with columns for in and out times. By performing an equal join with this view on an inpatient ENC and a theta join on a specific instant, you can retrieve a single row containing the patient's department, room, and bed at that moment. This view has been validated using ADT data from the EMR system's ADT application, and using interfaces to capture ADT data may lead to unexpected results.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE
  description: The V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE view provides details regarding medication orders dispensed from inpatient pharmacies, with each row representing a single medication dispense.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_DISPENSE_ACTION
  description: This view includes all actions related to the preparation and tracking of inpatient medication order dispenses.

— emr|dbo|V_PHARMACY_ORDER
  description: The V_PHARMACY_ORDER view provides details on medication orders that have been prepared or supplied by inpatient pharmacies, primarily for reporting purposes. Only orders that are signed and released or signed and held are included in this view.

— emr|reporting|IP_SEPSIS
  description: Staging table that holds inpatient sepsis screening results, encounter information, compliance metrics, and clinical observations for patients flagged for sepsis.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisDetails
  description: Comprehensive clinical information for sepsis cases, encompassing vital signs, laboratory results, medication administration timestamps, and organ dysfunction assessments.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisEncounters
  description: Records of inpatient sepsis encounters that include demographic information, admission and discharge timestamps, and diagnosis codes.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisEncountersWLocations
  description: Records of sepsis encounters that include ADT location history, detailing department transfers and their corresponding timestamps throughout the encounter.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisPatientDates
  description: A date-indexed view of sepsis patient encounters that includes aggregated department information for the purposes of trend analysis and compliance reporting.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisScreeningAudit
  description: Records of sepsis screening activities, which encompass organ dysfunction scores, huddle documentation, alert responses, and nursing assessments.

— emr|reporting|IP_SepsisShiftCompliance
  description: Data on sepsis screening compliance at the shift level, including breakdowns by AM/PM shifts, compliance rates, and the nursing staff responsible for the screenings.

— emr|reports|CONFIG_VALUE_SET
  description: This table serves as a configuration lookup, holding value sets utilized for department rollups, location groupings, and various reporting categories.

— emr|reports|FY_DATE_DIMENSION
  description: Table containing fiscal year date information, including fiscal year number, month, and corresponding calendar date mappings for aligning reporting periods.

— emr|reports|NON_SEVERE_SEPSIS_STAGING
  description: ETL staging table for identifying non-severe sepsis cases. Contains records of patients suspected of having sepsis but not qualifying for severe sepsis criteria.

— emr|reports|SEVERE_SEPSIS_STAGING
  description: ETL staging table for identifying severe sepsis cases. Contains records of patients who meet the criteria for severe sepsis along with tracking for compliance with bundle elements.
